claims.title: Diquis chiefdoms and the stone spheres
claims.summary: Chiefdom societies in the Diquis delta carve more than 300 near-perfect stone spheres and build settlements of mounds and paved precincts.

sources.label: Precolumbian Chiefdom Settlements with Stone Spheres of the Diquis
A Stone Sphere from Costa Rica

claims.title: UNESCO World Heritage inscription
claims.summary: The Diquis settlements with their stone spheres become Costa Rica's first cultural World Heritage Site, recognised as unique evidence of pre-Columbian chiefdom societies.

sources.label: Precolumbian Chiefdom Settlements with Stone Spheres of the Diquis

claims.title: Columbus reaches the Rich Coast
claims.summary: On his fourth voyage Columbus lands on the Caribbean coast; gifts of gold inspire the name Costa Rica, the Rich Coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1502-columbus-reaches-the-rich-coast, claim TL:CRI:event:1502:columbus-reaches-the-rich-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Cartago
claims.summary: The Spanish establish Cartago in the Central Valley as the colonial capital, which it remains until 1823.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1563-founding-of-cartago, claim TL:CRI:event:1563:founding-of-cartago, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from Spain
claims.summary: Central America, Costa Rica included, declares independence from Spain; the province soon joins the Mexican Empire and then a regional federation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1821-independence-from-spain, claim TL:CRI:event:1821:independence-from-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coffee arrives from Cuba
claims.summary: Thirteen years before independence, coffee is introduced and becomes the principal crop of a province that had never had one — a dominance lasting into the 20th century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1808-coffee-arrives-from-cuba, claim TL:CRI:event:1808:coffee-arrives-from-cuba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Juan Mora Fernandez, first head of state
claims.summary: Costa Rica's first elected head of state founds schools and courts and promotes coffee planting through free land grants.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1824-juan-mora-fernandez-first-head-of-state, claim TL:CRI:event:1824:juan-mora-fernandez-first-head-of-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Withdrawal from the federation
claims.summary: Disenchanted with the strife of the United Provinces of Central America, Costa Rica severs its federal ties and charts an independent course.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1838-withdrawal-from-the-federation, claim TL:CRI:event:1838:withdrawal-from-the-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Costa Rica declares itself sovereign
claims.summary: A decade after leaving the federation, the republic formally declares independence and notifies Washington on 5 September.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Costa Rica
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1848-costa-rica-declares-itself-sovereign, claim TL:CRI:event:1848:costa-rica-declares-itself-sovereign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: US recognition — on paper
claims.summary: Washington recognises Costa Rican independence by empowering its charge d'affaires in Guatemala, who never visits the country and reaches no agreement by post.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Costa Rica
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Diplomatic relations established
claims.summary: Costa Rican minister Felipe Molina presents his credentials in Washington; a US consulate opens in San Jose the following year.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Costa Rica
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: National War against William Walker
claims.summary: Costa Rica joins Central America in defeating the American filibuster William Walker; the soldier Juan Santamaria becomes a national hero.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1856-national-war-against-william-walker, claim TL:CRI:event:1856:national-war-against-william-walker, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Minor Keith and the banana railways
claims.summary: Minor C. Keith begins building railways and planting bananas, ventures that in 1899 merge into the United Fruit Company and reshape the Caribbean coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1872-minor-keith-and-the-banana-railways, claim TL:CRI:event:1872:minor-keith-and-the-banana-railways, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First free election in Central America
claims.summary: Costa Rica holds what is regarded as the first free and honest election in Central America, beginning a long democratic tradition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1890-first-free-election-in-central-america, claim TL:CRI:event:1890:first-free-election-in-central-america, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Disputed election sparks civil war
claims.summary: The annulment of the 1948 election to bar president-elect Otilio Ulate triggers a brief but bloody civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1948-disputed-election-sparks-civil-war, claim TL:CRI:event:1948:disputed-election-sparks-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Figueres leads the civil war
claims.summary: Jose Figueres Ferrer leads an armed uprising in support of president-elect Ulate; the two-month war kills about 2,000 people before the government surrenders.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1948-figueres-leads-the-civil-war, claim TL:CRI:event:1948:figueres-leads-the-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitution abolishes the army
claims.summary: Figueres's junta promulgates a new constitution that bans a standing army, grants women the vote, and nationalises the banks, then hands power to Ulate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1949-constitution-abolishes-the-army, claim TL:CRI:event:1949:constitution-abolishes-the-army, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: National park system created
claims.summary: Costa Rica establishes a national park system that grows to protect roughly a quarter of the country, anchoring its conservation and ecotourism economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1970-national-park-system-created, claim TL:CRI:event:1970:national-park-system-created, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oscar Arias wins the Nobel Peace Prize
claims.summary: President Oscar Arias Sanchez is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for the Central American peace plan signed by the region's leaders in August 1987.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1987-oscar-arias-wins-the-nobel-peace-prize, claim TL:CRI:event:1987:oscar-arias-wins-the-nobel-peace-prize, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A country without an army raises a force
claims.summary: After clashes with Sandinista troops across the San Juan, a US-trained anti-guerrilla force begins operating — the limits of demilitarisation in a region at war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-1985-a-country-without-an-army-raises-a-force, claim TL:CRI:event:1985:a-country-without-an-army-raises-a-force, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: San Juan navigation dispute settled
claims.summary: Costa Rica and Nicaragua resolve a long-standing quarrel over navigation on the river that forms their border.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-2000-san-juan-navigation-dispute-settled, claim TL:CRI:event:2000:san-juan-navigation-dispute-settled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Recognition switches from Taipei to Beijing
claims.summary: Costa Rica transfers diplomatic recognition to the People's Republic of China in pursuit of investment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-2007-recognition-switches-from-taipei-to-beijing, claim TL:CRI:event:2007:recognition-switches-from-taipei-to-beijing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Laura Chinchilla, first woman president
claims.summary: Costa Rica elects its first female head of state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-2010-laura-chinchilla-first-woman-president, claim TL:CRI:event:2010:laura-chinchilla-first-woman-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Diquis spheres named World Heritage
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribes the Diquis chiefdom settlements and their stone spheres as Costa Rica's first cultural World Heritage Site.

claims.title: The Hague settles Isla Portillos
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice rules that sovereignty over the disputed San Juan wetland belongs to Costa Rica — a demilitarised state settling its border in court.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Costa Rica: From the chiefdoms and stone spheres of the Diquis to a disarmed democracy of coffee, peace, and rainforest.", terralore.co/country/CRI/chronicle#ev-2015-the-hague-settles-isla-portillos, claim TL:CRI:event:2015:the-hague-settles-isla-portillos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
